newsitem.title: MEXICO: Northern Mexican bank Afirme sees Q4 loan growth.
newsitem.headline: Northern Mexican bank Afirme sees Q4 loan growth.

text.p: Banca Afirme, a small Mexican bank opened in this northern city last year, expects sharp loan growth toward the end of 1996, but year-end profits may dip slightly, a top official said on Wednesday.

Deputy Director General Victor Monroy of banking group, Afirme Grupo Financiero said in an interview that the bank's loan portfolio, that grew 280 million pesos between January and September, would hit 600 million pesos by the end of 1996.
"In the last quarter we are expecting an important expansion (in the portfolio)," he said.
Monroy said that being small and new, Afirme had been spared the bad-loan crisis that has hit its larger counterparts throughout Mexico since an economic crisis erupted in December 1994.
He said the bank had a past-due loan ratio of 0.001 to total loans, and a capitalisation index above 14 percent that he expected to remain around that level next year.
Average interest margins were 4.5 percentage points above the national average, he said. On loans to small- and medium-sized firms, he said margins reached eight percentage points.

Monroy said the bank was expected to achieve net profits of 55 to 60 million pesos in 1996, down slightly from last year's 65 milion pesos. At a group level, he saw year-end profits at 82 million pesos. He gave no comparative figure.

The bank has no plans to issue debt or equity in the near future, but it was expanding. In the last three months of 1996, Monroy said it would open up to four more branches in Monterrey at a cost of at least 500,000 pesos each.
In 1997, it planned to open an office in Mexico City, Puebla and Guadalajara, he added.
